title: rtcp: Strip padding if known before dissecting payload
description:
If the padding bit is set, check to see if this is the last
RTCP message (if not, add the expert info), and if it is (and
the padding length byte is there) subtract it from the packet
length, so that packet type with optional extensions of unknown
length (e.g., profile-specific extensions) don't consume the
padding as opaque bytes and then throw an exception trying to
add the padding a second time.

If the padding length byte at the end is not present don't retrieve
it, so that we throw an exception as late as possible. If the padding
length value is too large, we'll either throw an exception when
adding the opaque bytes or when processing the padding, either way
as late as possible too.

Fix #20597

notes.body: Even though it is not supposed to be here, the flag says it is, so we should accommodate for it, possibly optionally, IMHO.

I would assume that the reason we don't currently is to try to accommodate what [RFC 3550 mentions as](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3550#section-6.4.1)

> some early implementations that incorrectly set the padding bit on the first individual packet and add padding to the last individual packet.

(It's not clear to me if such early implementations set the padding bit on *all* individual packets, or just the first, in which case the current implementation still wouldn't dissect the padding and might still run into this issue. At least it would dissect more of the frame and then possibly run into this at the end of the frame instead of earlier.)

So there's at least two different types of buggy implementations that might exist , and I reckon to dissect as much as possible before possibly throwing an exception in each case might require a preference, as you say.
It would require some more changes to the dissector to bring the padding dissection inside the loop instead of at the end.
I added a commit to add such a preference and optionally have either behavior. We can squash them before committing.
Thanks, let me see what I can make of this...
Do you have any concerns left now?

commits_data.title: RTCP: Strip padding if known before dissecting payload
commits_data.message:
RTCP: Strip padding if known before dissecting payload

If the padding bit is set, check to see if this is the last
RTCP message (if not, add the expert info), and if it is (and
the padding length byte is there) subtract it from the packet
length, so that packet type with optional extensions of unknown
length (e.g., profile-specific extensions) don't consume the
padding as opaque bytes and then throw an exception trying to
add the padding a second time.

If the padding length byte at the end is not present don't retrieve
it, so that we throw an exception as late as possible. If the padding
length value is too large, we'll either throw an exception when
adding the opaque bytes or when processing the padding, either way
as late as possible too.

RFC 3550 6.4.1:
"padding MUST only be added to the last individual packet, and if padding
is added to that packet, the padding bit MUST be set only on that packet."

It also mentions "early implementations that incorrectly set the padding bit
on the first individual packet and add padding to the last individual packet."

The current default behavior is to accommodate those implementations and
not try to dissect padding (but add an expert info) when the padding bit
is set on individual packets before the last. Add a preference to
instead try to dissect padding that appears before the last individual
packet, accommodating a different type of buggy implementation.

The RTCP padding should now be removed before handing it to the
packet type handlers, so they don't need to remove it twice.
We can also make the rtcp_padding_set global have function scope.

Fix #20597
